description: llama-dash brand themes. Each theme defines an accent palette (500/700/300), status colors, and the identity hue/chroma used to derive the series ramp. Surfaces, text and radius are shared across all themes — only the accent and a few harmonizing status colors change per theme. The 'shared' block below documents those shared tokens; it mirrors src/styles.css and is not read at runtime.

themes.name: Sapphire
themes.description: The default. A deep, saturated blue with real presence — reads as precision equipment rather than a terminal. Distinct from the info channel, which sits on the cyan side.

themes.name: Phosphor
themes.description: The default. Reads as operator terminal — nginx, htop, green-on-black roots. Calm, technical, the safest pick.

themes.name: Amber
themes.description: Amber CRT terminals, cockpit displays. Warmer than green, still phosphorescent.

themes.name: Blueprint
themes.description: Cool, technical, slightly clinical. Like schematic blueprints and datasheets.

themes.name: Jade
themes.description: Blue-green without going green — closer to sea glass and deep water than to a terminal. Quiet, expensive, unmistakably not a status colour.

themes.name: Ember
themes.description: Burnt orange with real heat in it. The most characterful pick — warmer and more alive than any of the blues, still legible on a dark canvas.

themes.name: Coral
themes.description: Terracotta / burnt-orange. Warmer and more human than a tech green. Distinct in a field of blue/green dev tools.

themes.name: Orchid
themes.description: A clean pink-magenta with a violet lean. Younger and more expressive than ultraviolet, and unmistakably not a status colour.

themes.name: Ultraviolet
themes.description: Uncommon for dev tools. Reads as research / experimental — ML/AI-native without being sci-fi purple.

themes.name: Steel
themes.description: Financial-terminal blue. The professional, trustworthy default for data-heavy tools.

themes.name: Brass
themes.description: Old brass and lacquered instrument cases. Warmer and more metallic than amber, with the warning channel pushed to a deeper orange so the two never blur.

themes.name: Chartreuse
themes.description: Between green and amber. Aggressive, high-contrast, distinctive. More new-product energy than CRT-green nostalgia.

themes.name: Slate
themes.description: A near-neutral ramp with only a trace of blue. For operators who want the data to carry every bit of the colour.

themes.name: Monochrome
themes.description: The bold move: no accent. All signal comes from semantic status colors only. Most serious, most restrained.
